$comment: What a user gesture should route to. Most gestures pick a revision scope, and
the scope decides which stages run and what the result is compared against, so
getting it wrong means a gate checks the wrong baseline and passes work nobody
Two answers are not scopes. `reuse` means no revision is opened at all: the
user named a template that already exists and wants new content in it, which is
a file copy. `ambiguous` means one clarifying question comes first.
These fixtures are checked mechanically for shape only: every scope must exist
in config/pipeline.json, and every gate must be the one that scope declares.
Whether an agent ACTUALLY routes this way is a property of a live session and
is observed in the acceptance runs — building an LLM-in-the-loop CI to assert
it would test the model, not the harness.
The `why` field is the point of each case: most of them exist because the
obvious reading of the phrase is wrong.

cases.gesture: change the email to r.harris@example.com
cases.why: A field in <doc-kind>-data.json. If this needs Java, the template has content literals and the data-spec contract is broken.

cases.gesture: fix the typo in the summary paragraph
cases.why: Same surface as the email: text lives in the data file.

cases.gesture: use Material icons instead of Lucide
cases.why: The diff lands in asset-request.json; the Java that places the icon does not change.

cases.gesture: use Lato for the body text
cases.why: A font swap is an asset swap, even though it changes how most of the page looks.

cases.gesture: make it navy instead of teal
cases.why: A palette token. Cross-cutting, which is why it is reviewed against the reference rather than diffed against the parent.

cases.gesture: tighten the spacing throughout
cases.why: A spacing token, not a layout change — provided the values are tokens and not per-section literals.

cases.gesture: rename renderHeader to renderMasthead
cases.why: The render must come out byte-identical: AE == 0 on every page against the parent.

cases.gesture: extract the spec record into its own file
cases.why: Structure moves, pixels do not.

cases.gesture: upgrade GraphCompose to the next patch
cases.why: A dependency bump is a refactor until it is not: if the render moves, the gate fails and that is the finding.

cases.gesture: make the sidebar wider
cases.why: Geometry. Even a one-number edit changes the layout, so it is reviewed against the reference.

cases.gesture: add a certifications section
cases.why: New structure needs analysis and an architecture update, not just code.

cases.gesture: redesign the header
cases.why: The full chain: this is what the long scope is for.

cases.gesture: add another award to the awards list
cases.why: Reads like data-only, and is not: a list that grows can push the page and re-flow everything below it. The verification step exists for this case.

cases.gesture: swap the avatar for a different photo
cases.why: An asset, even though it is the most visible thing on the page; the regions that may differ are the ones that use it.

cases.gesture: make the table header darker
cases.why: theme-only if it is a palette token, visual-change if it means new row striping. The orchestrator must ask exactly one question rather than guess.

cases.gesture: make it look more professional
cases.why: No surface named at all. Ask what specifically should change before opening any revision.

cases.gesture: make a new proposal for Acme using northline-proposal
cases.why: Names a published template and supplies new content. The layout already exists and was already approved; instantiate the bundle and edit its data file. Reconstructing it would spend the whole loop to land near a layout that is on disk.

cases.gesture: here is my CV content, use mint-editorial-cv for it
cases.why: Content is data. Nothing about the template changes, so there is no revision to open and nothing to approve — the approval already happened.

cases.gesture: in northline-proposal, make the header taller and move the logo right
cases.why: Names a published template AND describes a layout change. Naming a template does not make it a reuse; what changes decides. The revision belongs in the project template.json names as sourceProject, never in the bundle — publish rewrites bundle sources from the revision, so an edit there is reverted.

cases.gesture: something like mint-editorial-cv but with two columns
cases.why: The template is a starting point, not the answer. A different column structure is a new layout, so this is a revision (or a new template) rather than a reuse.
